newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos sticks to 1997 inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos sticks to 1997 inflation target.

text.p: Despite a bumpy ride ahead for the next few months, Venezuela's inflation reduction target is on track, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.
"In April there was a small increase in inflation which will continue this month...All this is contemplated in the model of the IMF and ourselves," Matos told a news conference.
Consumer prices rose 2.4 percent in April, up from 1.6 percent in March.
Matos warned that the effects of a recent increase in the minimum salary and backlogged price increases for certain goods and services would see another inflation peak in May.

"The small peaks we have seen and will see will be absorbed by the productive sector which has a high level of idle capacity," Matos said. "But we have smashed the general inflationary tendency," he added.
The government has set a target of bringing inflation down from 103.2 percent in 1996 to about 30 percent this year.
The International Monetary Fund recently backed the government's 1997 inflation target provided it kept a tight rein on government spending.
